integrity: The all-parameter theorem is proved by an explicit finite-range counting argument. The bundled computation only checks the Parikh-signature implementation and small cases; it is not used to extrapolate the infinite result. Literature comparisons distinguish the global density question from later ternary characterizations.
scientific_limitations: The polynomial exponent is an upper bound obtained by independently bounding Parikh-matrix entries and is not claimed optimal. The theorem proves global sparsity, not a structural characterization of M-unambiguous words for alphabets of size at least four.
title: Unconditional polynomial sparsity of \(M\)-unambiguous words
